tasks.specification: Implement clamp(value, lower, upper) for integer inputs with lower <= upper. Return lower when value < lower, upper when value > upper, and value otherwise. Return an integer. Inputs outside this domain are not specified.

implementation.correct:
def clamp(value, lower, upper):
    return min(max(value, lower), upper)
implementation.buggy:
def clamp(value, lower, upper):
    return max(value, lower)

tests.valid:
from solution import clamp

assert clamp(-2, 0, 10) == 0
assert clamp(12, 0, 10) == 10
assert clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5
tests.conflicting:
from solution import clamp

assert clamp(-2, 0, 10) == 0
assert clamp(12, 0, 10) == 11
assert clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5

mutants.source:
def clamp(value, lower, upper):
    return max(value, lower)
mutants.requirement: Values above upper must return upper.

mutants.source:
def clamp(value, lower, upper):
    return min(value, upper)
mutants.requirement: Values below lower must return lower.

mutants.source:
def clamp(value, lower, upper):
    return lower
mutants.requirement: Values inside the interval must remain unchanged.

tasks.specification: Implement merge_intervals(intervals) where intervals is a list, possibly empty and in any order, of [start, end] pairs of integers with start <= end. Each pair denotes every integer from start to end inclusive. Two intervals must be merged when they share at least one integer or are adjacent, meaning one starts exactly one after the other ends; merging continues transitively until no two remaining intervals share or adjoin integers. Return the merged intervals as a list of [start, end] lists sorted by start, where each list covers the smallest start and the largest end of its merged members. Do not modify the input. Inputs outside this domain are not specified.

tests.valid:
from intervals import merge_intervals

assert merge_intervals([]) == []
assert merge_intervals([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10]]) == [[1, 6], [8, 10]]
assert merge_intervals([[1, 3], [4, 6]]) == [[1, 6]]
assert merge_intervals([[1, 3], [5, 6]]) == [[1, 3], [5, 6]]
assert merge_intervals([[1, 10], [2, 3]]) == [[1, 10]]
assert merge_intervals([[8, 10], [1, 2]]) == [[1, 2], [8, 10]]
tests.conflicting:
from intervals import merge_intervals

assert merge_intervals([]) == []
assert merge_intervals([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10]]) == [[1, 6], [8, 10]]
assert merge_intervals([[1, 3], [4, 6]]) == [[1, 3], [4, 6]]
assert merge_intervals([[1, 3], [5, 6]]) == [[1, 3], [5, 6]]
assert merge_intervals([[1, 10], [2, 3]]) == [[1, 10]]
assert merge_intervals([[8, 10], [1, 2]]) == [[1, 2], [8, 10]]

mutants.requirement: Adjacent intervals, where one starts exactly one after the other ends, must merge.
A merged interval keeps the largest end of its members, including when a later interval is contained in it.
Intervals may arrive in any order and the result must be sorted by start.
Intervals separated by at least one uncovered integer must remain separate.

tasks.specification: Implement evaluate_rpn(tokens) where tokens is a non-empty list of strings forming a valid reverse Polish notation expression over integers. Each operand token is a decimal integer literal, possibly with a leading minus sign such as "-7". Each operator token is one of "+", "-", "*" and "/"; it consumes the two most recently produced values, using the earlier value as the left operand and the later value as the right operand, and produces one value. Division is integer division that truncates toward zero, so 7 / 2 is 3 and -7 / 2 is -3; the right operand of a division is never zero. Return the single remaining value as an integer. Inputs outside this domain are not specified.

tests.valid:
from rpn import evaluate_rpn

assert evaluate_rpn(["3"]) == 3
assert evaluate_rpn(["2", "3", "*"]) == 6
assert evaluate_rpn(["5", "3", "-"]) == 2
assert evaluate_rpn(["7", "2", "/"]) == 3
assert evaluate_rpn(["-7", "2", "/"]) == -3
assert evaluate_rpn(["4", "13", "5", "/", "+"]) == 6
tests.conflicting:
from rpn import evaluate_rpn

assert evaluate_rpn(["3"]) == 3
assert evaluate_rpn(["2", "3", "*"]) == 6
assert evaluate_rpn(["5", "3", "-"]) == 2
assert evaluate_rpn(["7", "2", "/"]) == 3
assert evaluate_rpn(["-7", "2", "/"]) == -4
assert evaluate_rpn(["4", "13", "5", "/", "+"]) == 6

mutants.requirement: The earlier value is the left operand of subtraction and division.
Division truncates toward zero when the exact quotient is negative.
Division discards the fractional part instead of rounding to the nearest integer.

tasks.specification: Implement top_k_frequent(words, k) where words is a list of strings, possibly empty, and k is an integer with 0 <= k <= the number of distinct strings in words. Count how many times each distinct string occurs. Return a list of the k distinct strings with the highest counts, ordered by count from highest to lowest; strings with equal counts are ordered by their string value from smallest to largest, so the order never depends on where they appear in words. Return an empty list when k is 0. Inputs outside this domain are not specified.

tests.valid:
from ranking import top_k_frequent

assert top_k_frequent([], 0) == []
assert top_k_frequent(["b", "a", "b"], 1) == ["b"]
assert top_k_frequent(["b", "a", "b", "a", "c"], 2) == ["a", "b"]
assert top_k_frequent(["x", "y", "x", "z", "z", "z"], 3) == ["z", "x", "y"]
assert top_k_frequent(["apple", "pear", "apple", "fig", "pear", "apple"], 2) == ["apple", "pear"]
assert top_k_frequent(["q", "q"], 0) == []
tests.conflicting:
from ranking import top_k_frequent

assert top_k_frequent([], 0) == []
assert top_k_frequent(["b", "a", "b"], 1) == ["b"]
assert top_k_frequent(["b", "a", "b", "a", "c"], 2) == ["b", "a"]
assert top_k_frequent(["x", "y", "x", "z", "z", "z"], 3) == ["z", "x", "y"]
assert top_k_frequent(["apple", "pear", "apple", "fig", "pear", "apple"], 2) == ["apple", "pear"]
assert top_k_frequent(["q", "q"], 0) == []

mutants.requirement: Strings with equal counts are ordered by ascending string value.
Higher counts come before lower counts.
Counts reflect every occurrence of a string.
